title: Next Bigger for Chosen Values
statement:
You get an array row of distinct integers and an array picks. Every value in picks is also in row, and picks has no repeats.

For each value in picks, find where it sits in row and look to its right. Report the first value you meet that is larger than it, or -1 if there is none.

Return the answers in the order of picks.

examples.why: After 5 come 3 (smaller) and then 9. After 2 the very next value 7 is bigger. Nothing after 8.
Only 2 follows 3, and it is smaller. The answer is the first bigger value to the right, not the biggest, and not something to the left like 4.

constraints: Every value of picks appears in row
hints: Solve it for every value of row first; then answering picks is just a lookup.
Values that are still waiting for a bigger value to their right are always in decreasing order. Which structure keeps them like that?
Scan row with a stack of waiting values. When a new value arrives, pop every smaller waiting value: the new value is their answer. Store answers in a map.

explain.intuition:
Answer the question for all of row in one pass, then look up each pick. While scanning left to right, keep a stack of values that have not yet seen anything bigger. Those values are always in decreasing order from bottom to top: if a smaller one sat under a bigger one, the bigger one would already have answered it.

When a new value x arrives, every waiting value smaller than x has just met its first bigger neighbour, which is x. Pop them, record x as their answer, then push x to wait in turn. Each value is pushed once and popped at most once, so the whole scan is linear.
steps: Create an empty stack and an empty map next.
For each x in row: while the stack is not empty and its top is smaller than x, pop the top and set next[top] = x.
Values left on the stack have no bigger value to their right.
pitfalls: Returning the largest value to the right instead of the first larger one.
Answering in the order of row instead of the order of picks.
Scanning the stack with a nested loop for every value, which turns a strictly decreasing row into O(n²).

solutions.title: Find, then scan right
solutions.idea: For each pick, find its index in row and walk right until something bigger shows up.

solutions.title: Monotonic stack, then look up
solutions.idea: One pass with a decreasing stack gives the next bigger value for everything in row; a map answers each pick.

followups: The row is circular: after the last value you wrap around to the first. What changes?
Return how far away the next bigger value is instead of the value itself.
